title: Inventory service recovery: sabsa-component-realisation-simple
summary: One internal inventory service, a PostgreSQL database and twelve authorised warehouse operators.

scenario.name: Inventory service recovery
scenario.scope: One internal inventory service, a PostgreSQL database and twelve authorised warehouse operators.
scenario.drivers: Restore warehouse inventory updates within 30 minutes; data loss must remain below five minutes.
scenario.design: One application instance and a standby database in the existing managed platform.
scenario.cost: EUR 18000 implementation and EUR 6000 annual operation; one-year benefit EUR 32000, with a 25 percent adoption uncertainty.
scenario.risk: Database replication delay can lose updates; lag alert at 60 seconds and hourly recovery-point checks reduce likelihood.
scenario.operations: Warehouse operations owns support from 06:00 to 22:00; the platform duty engineer handles recovery escalation.

architecture_context.scope: One internal inventory service, a PostgreSQL database and twelve authorised warehouse operators.
architecture_context.baseline: Manual restoration misses the recovery objective by 18 minutes

architecture_drivers.driver: Restore warehouse inventory updates within 30 minutes; data loss must remain below five minutes.

architecture_viewpoints.description: Service owner delivers reconciled transaction processing
One application instance and a standby database in the existing managed platform.
Managed Linux runtime and PostgreSQL standby

architecture_relations.failure: Timeout after 5 seconds; retry twice with same event_id; then reject and alert
architecture_relations.trust_boundary: Application service identity to restricted database role

entities.name: Inventory service recovery
entities.responsibility: Accept authorised transaction requests and return durable IDs

entities.name: PostgreSQL ledger
entities.responsibility: Persist unique event IDs and reconciled balances

entities.name: Morgan Lee
entities.responsibility: Own restore rehearsal and incident escalation

architecture_evolution.target: Managed recovery with durable event IDs
